title: Scale out: identical stateless servers behind one address
caption: Clients only know the load balancer. Servers can be added, removed or fail without clients noticing.

steps.text: DNS now points at the load balancer. The app servers sit on private addresses that clients never see.
The LB spreads requests across the pool. Three servers give roughly three times the capacity, and you add a fourth when load grows.
Servers keep no session state of their own. Sessions and data live in shared stores, so any server can answer any request.
App 2 fails its health checks: the LB stops sending it traffic, and App 1 and App 3 absorb the load.
